newsitem.title: GERMANY: Majority of Germans against gold revaluation - poll.
newsitem.headline: Majority of Germans against gold revaluation - poll.

text.p: A slender majority of Germans are opposed to Bonn's plan to revalue Bundesbank gold reserves to help Germany qualify for European monetary union (EMU), according to the results of a poll published on Friday.

The survey, carried out by the DIMAP research institute for the newspaper Bild and the MDR television channel, found that 52 percent of the 1,100 Germans interviewed were against the plan, while 37 percent were in favour. Eleven percent had no opinion.

Bonn's efforts to use profits from a revaluation of the central bank's gold reserves brought it into open conflict with the Bundesbank, which said such tactics threatened its independence and were risky for the stability of EMU.

The two sides have agreed in principle on a revaluation of the bank's currency reserves but, according to a Bundesbank council member earlier on Friday, there was still no scope for a pay-out following a revaluation of its gold reserves.
